'''Mario Kasun''' (born April 5, 1980) is a Croatian former professional [[basketball]] player. He played at the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position.

==Professional career==
Kasun started playing basketball at a local club in [[Delnice]] when he was 14, before he started playing professionally with BC Zrinjevac in [[Zagreb]]. He was part of the 1998–99 Croatian junior team and the Croatian under-21 team in 2000.

After two seasons in the Zagreb club, and winning the Croatian Cup, in 2000 he moved to [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga University]] in the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]], but was subsequently suspended by the [[Croatian Basketball Federation]] for this abrupt move, and spent two seasons on the bench.

Kasun played at 2002 NBA pre-draft camp in [[Chicago]], being one of the tallest players, and showing some center skills. During 50 minutes over three games, he totalled 20 points and had 14 rebounds and six blocked shots, converting nine of 17 shots (52.9%).<ref name=NBA.com>[http://www.nba.com/draft2002/profiles/mario_kasun.html NBA.com: Mario Kasun<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> In 2002, he was initially selected by the [[National Basketball Association]]'s (NBA) [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in the second round (41st overall) of the [[2002 NBA draft]]. On June 26, he was traded by the Clippers to the [[Orlando Magic]] in exchange for future considerations. Regardless of this, he then moved to Germany to play for the [[Deutsche Bank Skyliners]], based in [[Frankfurt]]. With them he won the German championship and also appeared in the [[2003–04 ULEB Cup]].

===Orlando Magic===
In 2004, he returned to the US to play for the [[Orlando Magic]]. In the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05 season]] he played in 45 games for Orlando and averaged 7.9 minutes per game. In [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06]], he appeared in 28 games. Kasun's final NBA game was played on March 4, 2006, in a 94–110 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]] where he recorded 4 points in 4 minutes of playing time. Kasun averaged 2.7 points and 2.6 rebounds in a total of 73 games in his NBA career.

===FC Barcelona===
In July 2006 he returned to Europe again, signing a three-year contract with [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] led by head coach [[Duško Ivanović]] and general manager [[Zoran Savić]].

On 19 January 2008, during a [[2007–08 ACB season|Spanish League]] game away at [[CB Gran Canaria|Gran Canaria]], Kasun left the floor in a near-[[Syncope (medicine)|collapsed]] state while ===Efes Pilsen===
During the summer 2008 off-season, Kasun signed with [[Efes Pilsen S.K.|Efes Pilsen]].

In August 2010 he returned to [[Croatia]] and signed a one-year contract with [[KK Zagreb]].<ref>[https://thehoopsmarket.blogspot.com/2010/08/kk-zagreb-signs-mario-kasun-to-one-year.html KK Zagreb signs Mario Kasun to a one-year contract]</ref>

In August 2012 he signed a two-year contract with [[Montepaschi Siena]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/italy/serie-a/42626/mens-sana-siena-officially-adds-mario-kasun.html Mens Sana Siena officially adds Mario Kasun]</ref> In December 2012, Kasun left the team for personal reasons.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/104809/180/montepaschi-siena-center-kasun-part-ways Montepaschi Siena, center Kasun part ways]</ref> In September 2013, he signed with [[Al Wasl SC|Al Wasl Dubai]] for the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Al Wasl inks Mario Kasun|url=http://basketball.eurobasket.com/Croatia/news/334353|accessdate=30 September 2013|newspaper=Eurobasket.com}}</ref>

In 2014 he had to play for [[BC Levski Sofia|Levski Sofia]] another two seasons before retiring, but the club president was arrested for tax evasions just as he was due to sign for the club, so he never played for them.<ref>{{cite news|title=MARIO KASUN'U različitim su mi klubovima slomili ruku u istoj dvorani i isti me doktor uvjeravao da mi nije ništa. Bio sam u depresiji i htio se ubiti, a iz košarke sam se maknuo jer su mi se zgadili prevaranti'|url=https://100posto.hr/sport/u-razlicitim-su-mi-klubovima-slomili-ruku-u-istoj-dvorani-i-isti-me-doktor-uvjeravao-da-mi-nije-nista-bio-sam-u-depresiji-i-htio-se-ubiti-a-iz-kosarke-sam-se-maknuo-jer-su-mi-se-zgadili-prevaranti|accessdate=December 1, 2018|work=100posto.hr|date=November 4, 2018|language=Croatian|archive-date=December 1, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181201135124/https://100posto.hr/sport/u-razlicitim-su-mi-klubovima-slomili-ruku-u-istoj-dvorani-i-isti-me-doktor-uvjeravao-da-mi-nije-nista-bio-sam-u-depresiji-i-htio-se-ubiti-a-iz-kosarke-sam-se-maknuo-jer-su-mi-se-zgadili-prevaranti|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In February 2018 he played one match for KK Samobor, a regional division club from Croatia.<ref>{{cite news|title=Mario Kasun debitirao pobjedom u dresu Samobora|url=https://www.01portal.hr/sport/mario-kasun-debitirao-pobjedom-u-dresu-samobora|accessdate=December 1, 2018|work=01portal.hr|date=February 5, 2018|language=Croatian}}</ref>

==Croatian national team==
Kasun was part of the [[Croatia national basketball team]] at [[EuroBasket 2005]], [[EuroBasket 2007]] and [[EuroBasket 2009]]. After a disappointing result for Croatia in the Eurobasket 2009, Mario Kasun announced his retirement from the national team with this words: "This was my last game for the national team. Every time I gave everything on the court, but it seems that is not enough. I need the summer to rest and not be injured. Obviously I am not stable in the head anymore."<ref>[http://www.24sata.hr/sport/prka-i-kasun-oprostili-se-porazom-od-reprezentacije/136480/ Kasun goodbye] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090924183011/http://www.24sata.hr/sport/prka-i-kasun-oprostili-se-porazom-od-reprezentacije/136480/ |date=2009-09-24 }} {{in lang|hr}}</ref>

==Personal life==

In a March 2005 interview with ''[[Inside Hoops]]'', Kasun referred to [[Dražen Petrović]] as one of his favorite players and number one idol.<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/kasun-interview-030605.shtml InsideHoops.com – Mario Kasun Interview<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

In 2007, while playing professionally for [[FC Barcelona Basquet|FC Barcelona]], Kasun began dating the Spanish photographer Raquel Expósito, having reportedly met her at a Barcelona [[nightclub]].<ref name="story-kasun-2017">{{cite news|last=|first=|url=https://story.hr/Celebrity/a84427/PREKID-POZNATOG-PARA-Deset-godina-ljubavi-otislo-u-vjetar.html|title=Prekid poznatog para: Deset godina ljubavi otišlo u vjetar?|agency=Story.hr|archivedate=|archiveurl=|date=19 May 2017|access-date=4 July 2024}}</ref> The couple was [[engagement|engaged]] during summer 2008 and in early 2012 had a daughter, named Sade after the [[Sade (singer)|famous singer]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Carević|first=Ivana|url=https://www.vecernji.hr/showbiz/trudna-zarucnica-kosarkasa-kasuna-kcer-ce-nazvati-sade-348211|title=Trudna zaručnica košarkaša Kasuna kćer će nazvati Sade|agency=[[Večernji list]]|archivedate=|archiveurl=|date=20 November 2011|access-date=4 July 2024}}</ref> In 2017, after more than a decade together, the two split up.<ref name="story-kasun-2017"/>

Kasun is famous for his tattoos, of which he has 30, having gotten his first when he was only 15. His tattoos are mostly related with his faith and family. On his right forearm and wrist he has an angel and four letters: E, D, M and A. Those represent the first letter on the name of every member in his family: E for his sister "Eva", D for his father, "Drago" (angels, inner side of right [[biceps]]), M is meant for his own name, "Mario" and A for mother "Ankica" (right [[rib]]). On his back he has a big tattoo of another angel, which he describes as "watching my back".<ref name=24sata>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120526093035/http://www.24sata.hr/index.php?cmd=show_clanak&tekst_id=28462&_no_browse=1|title=Kasun's tattoos}} {{in lang|hr}}</ref>
